Sean / team — my initial legal position below (high level):

1) Defense control: we cannot accept a blanket allocation of defense control to the customer for "generated output" claims. That would require us to relinquish control over litigation strategy in areas where our platform operation is central. Proposed compromise:
   - Redwood will accept customer defense control only where (a) the claim arises solely from customer supplied inputs (prompts/data) and (b) customer indemnifies Redwood for Redwood's reasonable costs if customer mishandles defense.
   - For claims implicating platform operation, Redwood retains primary defense control but will cooperate and permit reasonable participation by the customer.

2) Evidence custody & retention: 7 years is above our current default retention and has material cost. Propose:
   - Default logs retention: 13 months (to align with current infra).
   - Extended retention addendum: up to 7 years at an agreed per‑GB/month fee or a flat per‑account surcharge.
   - Define scope: what we will provide (request/response text, model version, timestamps, routing metadata, user identifiers hashed/anonymized as required) vs what we will not provide (raw model weights, internal training data, non‑customer prompts).

3) Evidence SLA / turnaround: we can provide initial triage packet (sanitized request/response logs, model version, timestamps) within 48–72 business hours for high severity incidents; full handoff (including longer historical pulls and any manual redaction) within 30 calendar days. Any faster turnaround requires an Ops escalation path + fee or a contractual SLA credit for productivity loss.

4) Escrow / insurance threshold: recommend we ask for a minimum threshold (e.g., claims <$250k we handle under standard process; above that, customer may elect defense control if they meet an insurance/escrow requirement). This prevents frequent low‑value takeovers.

I'll prepare redline language that captures the carve‑outs and the optional retention addendum. Please flag any operational constraints so I can calibrate the turnaround commitments.

-Kimberly

Emma — thanks for the clear asks and for patience while we scoped internally. High level Redwood proposal below (we can put this into a redline / addendum):

1) Defense control: Redwood will retain primary defense control where claims implicate the platform or model operation. Customer may assume defense control only where the claim arises exclusively from Customer supplied inputs and Customer satisfies an insurance/escrow threshold (proposed threshold: $250k). If Customer assumes defense control, Redwood will require a holdback or indemnity for Redwood's reasonable litigation costs if mishandled.

2) Retention: Default retention remains 13 months. Extended retention up to 7 years available via a paid addendum; pricing to be provided once Ops provides sizing.

3) Evidence SLA: initial triage packet within 48–72 business hours for high severity incidents; full artifact production within 30 calendar days. If Acme requires a 5 business day initial SLA we can consider it as part of an SLA premium (we can offer a 10–15% recurring uplift or a one‑time fee for expedited handling).

4) Artifacts: we'll provide request/response text, model version, prompt metadata and routing logs. We will not disclose raw model weights or internal training datasets. KV cache snapshots provided only when necessary and with additional safeguards.
